heroLead: Open-source knowledge for better engineering decisions. Start from a real problem, reason through context and trade-offs, then implement a decision you can verify.
searchPrompt: What are you trying to decide?
aiPrompt: or think it through with an AI assistant that asks about context first

example.problem: Checkout API p95 went from 120 ms to 2.4 s.
example.context: Postgres, 40M orders, traffic doubled this quarter.
example.diagnose: pg_stat_statements: one query is 61% of DB time.
example.alternatives: Index · rewrite · Redis cache · bigger instance.
example.tradeoffs: An index is cheap and reversible; a cache adds stale data.
example.verify: p95 back to 140 ms; the plan shows an Index Scan.
example.learn: Cost grew with the table, not the traffic.

why.title: AI can write the code. The judgment is still yours.
why.body: Assistants generate code and answers in seconds. They can't know your context, weigh the trade-offs you'll live with, or own the decision. That is the skill this project trains.

course.label: Traditional learning
course.note: Teaches a tool before you have a reason to use it.

assistant.label: AI coding assistant
assistant.note: Fast answers. You inherit decisions you never made.

icestack.label: IceStack
icestack.note: Slower by minutes. You leave with the judgment, not just the code.

path.title: From problem to implementation
path.body: Start wherever you are. Most people arrive with a problem; the method, the patterns and the trade-offs are there for when the answer is “it depends”.

openSource.title: The repository is the source of truth.
openSource.body: Every page is a Markdown file on GitHub; the website is a better way to read it. Anyone can fix a mistake, add a trade-off or share a production lesson with a pull request.
openSource.sourceTreeCaption: Markdown in, website out: navigation, search and the reasoning path are generated from these files.
